title: A good intention, an unintended use
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Have you ever given someone something that they used in a way you never meant?

A student said: at the beginning I think it was very benevolent that they very quickly said: yes, we'll send out satellites. But it is understandable that he had some drawbacks when it started to be used for things other than humanitarian efforts.

I said: he thought he was doing something great, being useful, with great intentions. Then all of a sudden, people started putting the connections on drones to do assaults, and he found himself in a compromising position, because that wasn't the intention of giving them the connections.
I said that we don't have to get into all the details of the war, and I wanted to go into a deeper discussion about ethics in foreign problems like this.

groups.heading: A question for your own work

lines.text: What could your product or service be used for that you did not intend? Who would you have to ask before you hand it over?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you provide that someone could use in a way you didn't intend.
Write the worst use you can imagine.
Write who you would ask before you provide it.
Write what you would do if you found out later.
Write the condition you will attach.

check.q: What did I say the person's intention was in giving the connections?
choices: To do something great and be useful

check.q: What did I want to discuss?
What did the connections end up being used for, as I retold the book?

recap: Think about how what you provide could be used. Ask before you hand it over.
